prompts.text: What's the most useful skill you've learnt from watching somebody do their job?
Tell me about seeing an ordinary role differently after spending a day with someone who does it.
Learn how a trade is practised or follow a professional through a typical working day?
You're invited to observe a job you've never considered. What would you want explained before arriving?
The most demanding part of a job is often invisible to the people who receive its results.
A job title rarely tells you what someone enjoys about their work.
Which occupation would you like to understand beyond its public-facing tasks?
Recall somebody explaining a professional tool in a way that made it understandable.
A teenager asks you how your work actually helps other people. What example would you choose?
Hear how a professional started their career or what has surprised them since beginning?
What's a useful question to ask when you're exploring an unfamiliar career path?
Describe a conversation that changed your assumptions about a particular industry.
Find out which qualifications are essential or which practical experiences are most valuable?
A friend wants to leave one industry for another. What might they ask people already doing the work?
Career transitions often involve skills that people learnt without calling them transferable.
A career change needn't mean the previous years were wasted.
Which ability from your first job do you still use, even in a different role?
Tell me about someone whose unusual career journey gave you an idea for your own.
You're researching a role with many different job titles. How would you decide which descriptions are reliable?
Shadow a professional for an afternoon or attend a short introductory workshop?
How can you tell when a team welcomes questions from people who are still learning?
Recall a colleague who made it safe to admit you were unfamiliar with a process.
Get a detailed onboarding guide or a patient teammate who can answer questions as they arise?
A new employee joins a team where everyone uses unfamiliar abbreviations. How should coworkers help?
A welcoming workplace often reveals itself through the questions nobody is embarrassed to ask.
A manager's patience with beginners is more important than an impressive welcome speech.
What's one thing you wish you'd understood during your first week in a job?
Describe learning a workplace routine that everybody else took for granted.
You've been asked to welcome a teammate working remotely. What would you make sure they know?
Meet the team through short one-to-one conversations or a relaxed group introduction?
What's the hardest aspect of teamwork to explain to someone who's only worked independently?
Tell me about a shared project where a teammate's unusual strength became essential.
Plan a project together in detail or agree on outcomes and let people choose their methods?
Two teammates have different ideas about what finished work should look like. What could clarify expectations?
Teams often communicate a great deal through habits that were never written down.
A useful meeting needs a decision or shared understanding, not necessarily a full agenda.
What makes feedback from a colleague easier to act on?
Recall a work problem that was solved because somebody asked an overlooked question.
Your team discovers duplicated work shortly before a deadline. How would you organise a constructive review?
Receive specific feedback on a draft or observe somebody demonstrate a better approach?
What part of learning a new skill tends to frustrate people more than they expect?
Describe practising a skill long enough to notice a small but meaningful improvement.
Learn from a structured course or a series of practical mini-projects?
You have six weeks to become comfortable with a new tool. How would you structure the first few sessions?
People often overestimate what they can learn in one afternoon and underestimate gradual practice.
Being willing to practise awkwardly is part of becoming good at any professional skill.
Which skill would you most enjoy learning simply because it would make work more interesting?
Recall a teacher or colleague making a complex task suddenly feel manageable.
Two beginners learn the same software at different speeds. What would help them support each other?
Master one tool deeply or understand the basics of several tools that work together?
Which everyday workplace habit saves more time than people realise?
Tell me about simplifying a routine that used to involve unnecessary steps.
Organise your tasks by urgency or by the concentration each one requires?
A team has three different places where it records decisions. How might they choose one consistent approach?
A small improvement to a repeated process can matter more than a dramatic one-time change.
The best productivity method is one people will actually maintain.
Which work habit became more valuable as your responsibilities increased?
Recall discovering that a familiar task could be done more reliably with a checklist.
Your workday keeps being interrupted by small requests. What information would help you redesign it?
Use short focus periods with breaks or reserve a longer block for complicated tasks?
What makes a workplace mentor particularly helpful at the beginning of a career?
Describe advice you received that only made sense after you gained more experience.
Ask a mentor how they handled early mistakes or what they wish they'd learnt sooner?
A junior colleague asks for career guidance but has very different ambitions from yours. What would you clarify first?
Good mentoring can involve learning from someone who has less formal experience in a particular field.
Useful advice should help a person make their own decision instead of copying the mentor's path.
Which professional lesson would you gladly pass on without turning it into a rule?
Recall helping someone new discover an approach that suited their strengths.
Two people in your workplace want mentoring but need different things. How could you set expectations?
Meet a mentor regularly to discuss goals or ask for feedback only when specific challenges arise?
What does a healthy working relationship look like when teammates rarely meet in person?
Tell me about collaborating successfully with someone who lived in another city.
Use a shared written project board or frequent short team calls?
A remote colleague misses important context because decisions happen in the office. How should the team adapt?
Remote collaboration can make clear writing more important than informal hallway conversations.
A video call isn't automatically more effective than a carefully written update.
Which communication habit helps you trust colleagues you seldom meet face to face?
Recall a time a detailed handover prevented an avoidable misunderstanding.
A teammate in another time zone needs an answer while you're offline. What could make your documentation useful?
Have a predictable daily update or a weekly discussion focused on major decisions?
How do you decide when a job is teaching you something valuable versus simply keeping you busy?
Describe an early work responsibility that helped you understand your strengths.
Choose a role with varied responsibilities or one with a clear specialist path?
A friend is offered a promotion that includes work they don't enjoy. What should they investigate?
A job can become more satisfying when a person understands the purpose behind routine tasks.
Professional success isn't always best measured by how quickly someone changes titles.
Which part of your working life would you like to understand more clearly before setting your next goal?
Recall discovering a kind of work you enjoyed more than you'd predicted.
You're reviewing the last year of your career. Which experiences would you study besides your achievements?
Focus next on learning something difficult or on making an existing strength more useful?
Which quality makes you willing to recommend somebody for a professional opportunity?
Tell me about meeting a reliable collaborator through a casual community event.
Introduce two people through a shared project or through a short informal conversation?
Someone asks you to recommend a colleague for work outside your expertise. What would you want to know?
Professional networks often grow through people remembering helpful and dependable behaviour.
Networking doesn't have to involve trying to get something from every conversation.
What has made a professional introduction feel thoughtful rather than transactional?
Recall learning something useful from a person you only met once at an event.
Two colleagues might benefit from knowing each other but have never met. How would you introduce them?
Join a professional community to exchange skills or attend small talks with people from other fields?
